# YM02: 勤政亲贤 Qinzheng Qinxian, "Diligent in Government and Friendly with Officials"

Malone calls it Hall of Diligent Government.

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM02` · Page: `/scenes/#YM02` · Row: `research/buildings/YM02-qinzheng-qinxian/`

## What it was

勤政亲贤 Qinzheng Qinxian is the working court east of the audience hall: the five-bay 勤政殿, where the emperor read memorials and saw officials until noon (S05 j80:11b, 17b-18a; E1066, E1039), and east of it a cluster of small halls, a pavilion and courts: 飞云轩, 静鉴阁, 怀清芬, 秀木佳荫, 生秋庭, 芳碧丛, the three-bay 保合太和殿, the storeyed 富春楼 and 竹林清响 (j80:19a-20a, E1067). Malone calls it a smaller audience hall with adjacent courts (S02 p.77, E1082). It stayed in daily use to the end: audiences in the hall in summer and in the east study in spring and autumn (S211, E1088), and Xianfeng kept mourning for his father in 飞云轩 in 1850 (S207, E1089). It burned in October 1860 with the core of the garden; S50 says the gate and three courts of the neighbouring 吉祥所 survived (E1083, a lead).

From the inventory row: **changed** Differs between album and later Yangshi Lei plans (S41, no details); **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S41, S01, S310).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Leaf 2 of the 1744 album (P0002). Qianlong's preface (S40, E1039; S05 j80:17b-18a): east of the audience hall is 勤政殿, '日於此披省章奏召對臣工亭午始退' ('daily here I read memorials and summon officials, leaving only at noon'), with the 無逸 written on the screen behind the seat; further east 保合太和 among fine rocks and flowers, bright courts, linked pavilions and paths through trees. The poem is a pledge of diligence: no rest by day or night, every word weighed.

### How later sources differ

Qianlong added to the plaque 为君难 a colophon and poems of 1759 and 1785, Jiaqing a poem of 1801 and Daoguang a note of 1823 (S360, E1072); the court is listed among the scenes whose later plans differ from the album (S41; the rule in research/questions.md under Q1), so S01 wins on layout. No dated rebuilding was found in the texts read.

Sheets: 样002-3 踏勘勤政殿东书房尺寸底 of 咸丰五年三月 1855 (E1084), figures behind the paywall; 样002-17 保合太和 (undated), whose slip gives three bays of 3丈6尺 and 2 x 3丈2尺 (32.0 m), depth 3丈6尺, a three-bay front porch 2丈2尺 deep, columns 1丈4尺: each bay subdivided into three on the facade, so it reads as nine (S310 rec. 10368). 勤政殿 itself: five bays with three-bay 抱厦 front and back (S310 rec. 7310). Lei family 烫样 of 勤政殿 exist, of the Tongzhi repair (S920).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

S05 j80:12a-b and 19b-20a list the fittings: the plaque 勤政亲贤 and the rear plaque 为君难 by Yongzheng, Qianlong's couplets front and rear, the 无逸 on the throne screen, and on the rear walls Qianlong's two essays on ruling written out by 梁诗正 (east) and 于敏中 (west); in 保合太和殿 the Four Admonitions on the wall and plaques in the west warm room; in 富春楼 four plaques downstairs. S211 adds the working arrangement: three bays of folding doors opened, a partition front and back, an east study without a porch with its door to the east (E1088).

- **Q41. 藏密楼 YM31-07, 松风阁 YM81.** 百景图志 and the site stone put them in 平湖秋月; S337 and S111 put 君子轩-藏密楼 (1758) under 涵虚朗鉴 on the north shore. Two against one. 富春楼 YM02-09: Qianlong's note of 1794 says it stands before 镂月开云 (S360 p.109), the compilation files it under 勤政亲贤.
